title: Distributive Adjectives Vs Pronouns
theory:
1 Each/ Every/ Either/ Neither/ Each and Every + Singular Noun + Singular Verb + ..... + Singular
 Adjective + .....
 2 Each of/ Either of/ Neither of/ Any of + Plural Noun + Singular Verb + .....+ Singular Adjective + .....

  Either – One of the two. (nks esa ls dksbZ ,)
  Neither – Not one nor the other. (nks esa ls dksbZ Hkh ugha)
  Each – One by one (Individual focus) (nks ;k nks ls ”;knk esas ls gj ,). It can be used for two or
 more than two.
  Every – All members as a group (Collective sense). (lHkh) It is used for more than two only. It is
 only a determiner; therefore, we cannot use ‘of ’ after every.
  Each and every – Strong emphasis every individual member. (gj , & ^tksj nsdj*). It is used
 for more than two only.
  Any – It means one out of more than two. (nks ls ;knk esa ls dksbZ ,)
  None – Not any of more than two. (nks ls ;knk esa ls dksbZ Hkh ugha)
